newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent seen 5 cents down, gas oil unchanged.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent seen 5 cents down, gas oil unchanged.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were called to open 5 cents lower on Wednesday on the back of lower crude numbers on after-hours ACCESS trade while gas oil was expected to open unchanged, brokers said.
One broker also cited American Petroleum Institute (API) data released after the market closed on Tuesday, which he said showed a higher-than-expected build in crude oil stocks.
September Brent closed 12 cents higher on Tuesday at $18.22 a barrel after news from the United Nations indicated that a resumption of Iraqi oil exports was unlikely within the next few weeks.

Brokers said a move lower in overnight electronic trade and a report by the American Petroleum Institute (API) showing higher-than expected crude stocks for the week ended July 18, was likely to pull Brent lower.
"Brent should open around 5.0 cents down on Access and the API," one broker said.
NYMEX September futures trading on ACCESS was last traded at $19.41 a barrel, down seven cents.
IPE August gas oil was anticipated to open at Tuesday's settle of $163 a tonne.

The API data showed U.S. crude stocks in primary storage rose by 1.42 million barrels for the period, compared with market expectations of shortfall of around 3.0 million barrels. But market analysts in the U.S. said the implied rise in gasoline demand of 8.88 million barrels per day may fuel a near-term upward move.
London dealers said the market was likely to hold in a range as it awaited further news on the timing of resumed Iraqi oil exports, now seen not likely for several weeks.
"No-one wants to trade while Iraq is up in the air. We're in a very narrow trading range. The volumes say it all," a broker said.
A U.N. spokesman on Tuesday said the approval of Iraq's aid distribution plan, which Iraq insists on before it resumes exports, was not expected until the end of July.
Iraq needs to sell around 1.5 million barrels of crude per day to raise the $1 billion it needs to buy humanitarian aid before the deal ends in September.
The second phase of the oil-deal started on June 8.
